business.body: The Company is engaged in the manufacturing and marketing of textile products, garments, technical textiles and allied products, serving both domestic and international customers. Terry towels and made-ups remain its principal business, supported by an artificial leather (technical textile) operation and an agency division that acts as consignment stockist of GAIL (India) Limited for polymer marketing and distribution in Rajasthan. It has established long-standing relationships with reputed overseas buyers that contribute repeat business.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named expansion project, commissioning timeline or capex quantum. The only forward-looking expansion signal is the Board's decision to withhold a dividend for FY 2025-26 "considering the future expansion plans", without describing those plans. The existing footprint comprises the manufacturing facility at Kotputli, Rajasthan (RIICO Industrial Area, Village & Post Keswana, plots SP-4/3, SP-4/3A and SP-3-5-B, District Jaipur) with an installed capacity of approximately 6,200 MTPA for terry towels and 100 lakh metres for synthetic PU/PVC leather, plus a stitching unit and the agency division operating from VKI, Jaipur. Growth intent is stated qualitatively rather than as projects: expansion into new export geographies to reduce dependence on traditional markets, growth in the artificial leather segment with increased focus on exports and the automobile sector (which management says should ramp up operations in that segment in coming years), and addition of new textile customers. Separately, the AGM notice seeks member approval for a corporate guarantee not exceeding Rs. 3,50,00,000 at a 0.5% p.a. guarantee commission to secure a bank guarantee sanctioned by HDFC Bank Limited to related party M/s. Suave Casa Ideas Private Limited.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for home textile products remained subdued, particularly in the United States, owing to inflationary pressures, cautious consumer spending, inventory rationalisation by large retailers and uncertainty from U.S. tariff policy changes
- The decline in revenue and profitability was primarily attributable to the adverse impact of tariff measures imposed by the U.S. Government, which affected export demand, pricing realisations and business sentiment
- Textile division export volumes fell, particularly in the U.S. market; stable operating profitability was nonetheless maintained through improved cost efficiencies and moderation in raw material costs
- Technical textile (artificial leather) performance fell on subdued demand from end-user industries, mainly footwear and automobile, plus intense competition from low-cost products
- Improved profitability of the artificial leather business supported overall operating margins
- Long-term industry fundamentals remain favourable, supported by increasing urbanisation, rising disposable incomes, growing housing and hospitality sectors and rising preference for premium and sustainable home textile products
- Outlook for the textile industry remains positive, supported by growing domestic consumption, increasing export opportunities, government initiatives promoting manufacturing and a gradual shift towards value-added textile products
- Technical textiles continue to emerge as a significant growth driver for Indian manufacturers
- Management expects stability in operations through diversification of customer base and export destinations, improved operating efficiencies and sustained focus on value-added products
- Growth in the artificial leather business, prudent working capital management and strengthening customer relationships are expected to support future performance
